intro.title: Implement RequireAtLeastOne type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom TypeScript utility type called RequireAtLeastOne. This type ensures that at least one property from a given set is present in an object, making it more flexible than requiring all properties. You will learn to use mapped types and conditional types to iterate over keys and construct the required type. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system features like unions and the keyof operator. By the end, you will understand how to create precise type constraints for your objects.
intro.usecase: The RequireAtLeastOne type is essential in TypeScript applications where you need flexible but validated configurations. In dashboard settings, you might have optional display properties where at least one must be selected—like requiring either a chart type or data source to be specified. Form validation often uses this pattern when users must provide at least one contact method (email OR phone) while keeping other fields optional. API request builders benefit from it by ensuring query parameters include at least one filter criterion without mandating all possible filters.
